request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,
flag, list and line: in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates, the summary, and
any panel added later unless its request says otherwise) is shown as it stood at the end of the last
day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's today was on or before the as-of
date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,

date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The as-of view is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all four tests (the main as-of test and scenarios 1–3).

**How it works**
- **Screen:** a new control next to "Today" has an `asof-date` entry, an `asof-set` button, an `asof-clear` button and a `sheet-asof` value (empty when none is set). The date is kept in the URL (`asof`), so it belongs to that user's screen and nobody else's.
- **Reads:** while it's set, every request the screen makes for today, people, claims, rates, settings, periods and watches carries `?asOf=…`. The server rebuilds each answer from history in `asof/AsOfView.java`: only changes made while the sheet's today was on or before that date count, and the latest of each wins. The today endpoint returns the as-of date as "today", so overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements and the grade and rate in force are all worked from it. The screen's own calculations didn't need to change.
- **Changes:** `api/http.ts` refuses every change request while an as-of date is set, so each form shows its usual error. Nothing reaches the server, so the store and the audit file are untouched.

**New history** (migration `V46__as_of_view.sql`)
- The existing V45 history (claims, rates, dated settings, policy date, grades, holds, retirements) didn't cover everything on screen. The migration adds history for:
  - claim number, note, proofs, split-from and late-entry
  - person name and terms
  - statements, with when each was taken and cancelled
  - patrons and watches
  - periods being added, closed, soft-closed and reopened
  - archiving
  - the undated settings: roles, permissions, numbering, grace days and delegations
- Cancelling a statement now marks it cancelled instead of deleting the row. The live queries skip cancelled rows, so the live screen behaves as before.

**One fix outside the request:** scenario 2 failed on a plain statement right after a refused statement-as-of. The statement's date field kept the refused date, so the next statement was sent with it and refused again. That bug was already in the app. AGENTS.md says a value typed for a refused submission must not carry into the next one, so `StatementButton.tsx` now clears the date after each attempt, whether it's taken or refused.

**Limits:**
- Claims under an as-of date are listed in today's order, not the order they had then; this only differs if a claim was reassigned after that date.
- Opening a claim's editor while an as-of date is set shows an error, because opening it takes a lock and that counts as a change.
